decision.summary: The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to a target of 1-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1-1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed increased the federal funds rate by 25 basis points, moving it up from 1 percent to 1-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Although incoming inflation data are somewhat elevated, a portion of the increase in recent months appears to have been due to transitory factors.
changes.explanation: Policymakers noted that recent inflation data are somewhat elevated, but believe part of the rise is only temporary.

changes.quote: With underlying inflation still expected to be relatively low, the Committee believes that policy accommodation can be removed at a pace that is likely to be measured.
changes.explanation: The language shifted to emphasize that underlying inflation remains relatively low, allowing the Fed to remove policy support at a measured pace.

tone_quotes.quote: The Committee believes that, even after this action, the stance of monetary policy remains accommodative and, coupled with robust underlying growth in productivity, is providing ongoing support to economic activity.
Nonetheless, the Committee will respond to changes in economic prospects as needed to fulfill its obligation to maintain price stability.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 12.67% APR, a 25 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.62% and moved -8 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.32% would fall by about $15.63 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 5.6%, and employers added an average of 292k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.9% over the past year (May 2004); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 2.3% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.

card.whats_next: The statement signals that future rate hikes are likely to continue at a measured pace as long as inflation stays low. This educational forecast suggests the Fed will keep normalizing policy step-by-step at upcoming meetings.
